summary: Defines and partially implements the Singular keyword (issue #202): restricts simultaneous in-play copies of the same-named card to one per controller, without Unique's own additional one-per-deck-construction limit. Generalizes QuotePurchase's pre-existing Unique in-play-duplicate check into a shared ControlsCopyOf(owner,name) helper covering both keywords, and wires it at all three entry-into-play paths: QuotePurchase (Personality/Holding), the ordinary Equip() (Follower/Item/Spell), and equip-battle (Spell/Reserve) -- the latter two had NO such check at all before this, for either keyword, a real pre-existing gap found and fixed while generalizing. Six new training fixtures (training-unique-personality/-follower/-spell, training-singular-personality/-follower/-spell) demonstrate all three paths for both keywords; no real card wired yet (the 16 real Singular-carrying catalogue cards are mostly Regions, not built, plus two Personalities each blocked on an unrelated gap). Per the user's own spec, Unique also gets a new stated restriction -- may not take control of a second Unique/Singular copy, plus a unit-wide uniqueness check on capturing an enemy Personality's whole unit -- but both depend on a control-transfer mechanism that doesn't exist anywhere in the engine yet; recorded as a durable decision (docs/decisions/2026-09-12-unique-singular-control-transfer.md) rather than guessed at or half-built ahead of a real driving card. Rules-only touch to src/L5R.Core (CardAbilities.cs/CardCatalog.cs/MatchEngine.cs) plus tests and docs -- no client/UI files touched, so this crosses no actual lane boundary despite the file count; marked shared only because it spans engine + docs + a decision record in one PR.
validation: dotnet build (0 warnings/errors); dotnet run --project tests/L5R.Core.Tests -> 114/114 core (new UniqueAndSingularInPlayRestriction covers all three entry paths for both keywords, plus Unique's own previously-untested Purchase-path behavior) + 34/34 published + 8/8 deck-format; python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/content -> 121/121; python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/collaboration -> 43/43.
remaining: The control-transfer-dependent half of the user's own spec (take-control restriction; unit-wide capture check) is recorded as a durable decision but not implemented -- no control-transfer primitive exists yet to attach it to. When one is built, that PR must incorporate the decision doc's rule and then mark it superseded.
